checks: The lifted hull projects to [−1,1], so there are exactly three possible integer sites. Extremality fixes the endpoint fibers. At base zero, the endpoint weights agree, yielding a combination of K with RK and hence no enlargement. The original middle body is retained exactly.

Reflection across (0,0) pairs opposite closed through-origin caps. Boundary mass is included in both sides, so either side has at least half the total. A pair with nonzero continuous normal has a d-volume-null common boundary on each fiber and bounds every candidate by half the total. This proves both middle and global raw maxima.

Componentwise Minkowski interpolation changes only the radius and interpolates it linearly. Differentiation of (1+R^d/2)^q yields the displayed qd/2 factor and bracket (d−1)+(dq−1)R^d/2. At q=1/d this is strictly positive for d≥2. On 1≤R≤1+1/(2d), the binomial bound R^d<2 gives positivity even after replacing q by zero in the bracket.

Exact rational replay checked the radius bound and positive lower bracket for d=2 through 64, as well as the planar values 3/2, 3, 11/2. Squaring the proposed planar root inequality leads to 5≥√33, contradicted by 25<33.
Read 239caf8af54c6294 §8, (14)–(17). The normalized maximum is constant at 1/2. The strict failure concerns raw depth powers.

summary: The complete three-fiber centrally symmetric construction has optimized raw depth exactly half its mass. The dependence of that mass on the central radius gives the strict counterexamples for all positive powers.
